title: Playlist and Homecoming
premise: Paloma Thornbury, a scholarship student at Marrowgate Academy, has spent two years invisible — until his best friend Theo vanishes overnight, leaving behind a locker key and a half-finished playlist titled 'Homecoming.' Following the songs like breadcrumbs, Paloma uncovers a secret society of staff and legacy students who 'curate' which students get to belong, erasing the ones who don't. To expose them, he must survive two championships: the rowing regatta that keeps his scholarship alive, and the final music audition where the playlist's last song must be performed before the whole school. In the end, Paloma finds Theo hiding in the boathouse with proof of everything, wins neither trophy but both battles, and learns that belonging isn't granted by an academy — it's built by the people who refuse to let you disappear.
about_author: Ada Nystrom is a former boarding-school music teacher who writes stories about quiet kids with loud hearts. She lives in a coastal town full of boathouses, and she still makes playlists for people she loves.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet him navigating Marrowgate's social hierarchy: invisible by design, one wrong grade from losing his scholarship. His only anchor is Theo, a loud, golden boy who adopted him freshman year. Emotional beat: the fragile safety of staying unseen.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Theo doesn't show up to first period, then doesn't answer texts. By evening, his parents report him missing; police call it a runaway. Paloma is the last person who saw him. POV alternates between Paloma and Theo's sister, Junie. Beat: dread settling in.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Junie gives Paloma the single key found in Theo's room. It opens locker 114 — unassigned, welded shut for years — containing a phone and a playlist called 'Homecoming,' thirteen songs, each dated going forward. Beat: the mystery becomes personal.

chapters.title: Track One: Static
chapters.summary: The first song leads Paloma to the old auditorium, where he finds Theo's hidden notes about 'the Committee' — staff who decide which students belong. He's spotted by Wren, a scholarship girl who's been watching the same trail. Beat: fear mixed with the first spark of alliance.

chapters.title: Wren Knows Things
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She reveals her brother was 'asked to leave' two years ago after questioning the Committee. Together they map the playlist dates against school events. Beat: grief reframed as purpose; found family begins forming.

chapters.title: The Regatta Clause
chapters.summary: Coach Delacroix warns Paloma that his scholarship rides on winning the spring regatta — and that the Committee can revoke it with a signature. Training montage chapters begin. Beat: pressure mounting on every front at once.

chapters.title: Track Four: The Boathouse Tape
chapters.summary: A song date points to the boathouse, where Paloma finds a recording of a Committee meeting naming students to be 'managed.' His own name is on next year's list. Beat: cold terror — invisibility was never protection.

chapters.title: Legacy
chapters.summary: POV of Cassius Vane, legacy student and Committee heir, who suspects Paloma knows more than he should. Cassius isn't cruel so much as terrified of losing his own place. Beat: humanizing the antagonist system.

chapters.title: Practice Makes Pressure
chapters.summary: Rowing training intensifies while Paloma decodes tracks in stolen hours. Junie joins the investigation officially, posing as a transfer student. Beat: exhaustion, camaraderie, small victories.

chapters.title: The Erased Yearbook
chapters.summary: In the archives, they find yearbooks with faces cut out — students scrubbed from Marrowgate's memory entirely. One photo has Theo's face half-torn already. Beat: horror of institutional forgetting; theme of memory crystallizes.

chapters.title: Track Nine: Someone Follows
chapters.summary: Paloma realizes someone has been retracing his steps. A near-miss in the library stacks ends with him losing the phone — but not before memorizing track ten's location. Beat: paranoia, stakes raised.

chapters.title: Cassius Offers a Deal
chapters.summary: Cassius corners Paloma: help the Committee find what Theo left behind, and his scholarship is guaranteed forever. Paloma stalls. Beat: temptation and loyalty colliding.

chapters.title: Midnight Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Paloma, Wren, and Junie practice the audition piece in the empty chapel — the playlist's final song, unfinished, needing a second voice. They realize it's written for two. Beat: warmth; the trio becomes a true team.

chapters.title: Regatta Day
chapters.summary: Paloma rows the race of his life. He loses by half a length — deliberately sabotaged by a swapped seat assignment — and watches his scholarship status flicker into question. Beat: devastating public defeat.

chapters.title: The Committee Moves
chapters.summary: With Paloma marked for expulsion, Wren reveals she's been feeding information to a sympathetic teacher, Ms. Okafor, who once escaped the Committee herself. Beat: allies in unexpected places; hope rekindled.

chapters.title: Track Twelve: Where the Water Goes
chapters.summary: The second-to-last song leads to the storm drain beneath the boathouse — and to Theo himself, alive, hiding with a hard drive of evidence. He stayed hidden because coming forward meant trusting someone. He chose Paloma. Beat: reunion, catharsis.

chapters.title: What Theo Saw
chapters.summary: Theo's POV flashback: how he discovered the Committee erasing students, why he ran, and why the playlist was his lifeline back. Beat: the missing friend becomes a full person; guilt and relief intertwine.

chapters.title: The Plan Before the Audition
chapters.summary: The four plan to play the finished song at the spring audition, with the evidence cued to broadcast mid-performance. Ms. Okafor will be in the audience. Every ally is placed. Beat: tense preparation, ticking clock.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Paloma takes the stage before the entire school and the Committee. Mid-song, the recording plays; the erased names scroll across the hall screens. The room goes silent, then erupts. Beat: climax — art as exposure, courage as chorus.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Investigations begin; Cassius, given a choice, testifies against his own family. The headmaster resigns. Paloma's scholarship is reinstated — not as charity, but because students demand it. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: At the rescheduled homecoming dance, Paloma, Theo, Wren, and Junie perform the song together, finishing the playlist live. The thirteenth track plays over the speakers: it was always meant for this night. Beat: joy, belonging chosen and earned.

chapters.title: Thirteen Songs, No Silence
chapters.summary: Epilogue, months later. Paloma writes a new playlist — track one blank, waiting — and pins a photo of all four friends inside locker 114, now a memorial to every erased student restored. Beat: memory kept alive; the story closes on openness, not endings.
